hero.name: Salomon Kabongo
hero.lede: I research how machines learn language — and I teach it in English, French, Lingala and Tshiluba.
hero.description: My work sits between two things that rarely meet: peer-reviewed NLP research, and getting that knowledge to the people it was never written for. I build language technology for African languages, ship applied AI in industry, and explain both on YouTube.
hero.now_role: Lead Software Engineer, Innovation Group at State Farm
hero.now_phd: PhD in Computer Science, Leibniz Universität Hannover
hero.now_masakhane: Former Board Member, Masakhane Research Foundation

about.title: Language technology for the people it usually skips
about.bio1: I hold a PhD in Computer Science from Leibniz Universität Hannover, where my research focused on natural language processing, information extraction and knowledge graphs — specifically, how to pull structured, comparable claims out of the scientific literature at scale.
about.bio2: At State Farm's Innovation Group I lead applied research in computer vision, document intelligence and generative AI, work that has produced one issued AI/ML patent and three further filings. On the Masakhane Research Foundation board I helped drive a $9M+ programme building open NLP infrastructure for over a billion African language speakers.
about.bio3: The research and the teaching are the same project. A paper that only circulates among people who already read English is a paper that has not finished its job — which is why I teach in English, French, Lingala and Tshiluba.
research_items: Natural language processing & large language models
Speech recognition and translation for low-resource languages
about.darakili: That conviction is also why I work on DarAkili, a STEM education platform where African professionals publish free mini-courses in their own languages.

speaking.home_subtitle: I speak to research audiences and general ones, in English or French, on AI research, African language technology, and what it takes to build both.
speaking.title: Speaking
speaking.subtitle: I give talks to universities, research groups, conferences and companies — in English or French, remote or in person.
speaking.topic_1_title: Where large language models actually fail
speaking.topic_1_desc: A working researcher's account of what current systems do well, where they break, and how to tell the difference — pitched at a technical audience without assuming NLP expertise.
speaking.topic_2_desc: Why over a billion speakers remain underserved by language technology, what Masakhane and the wider community have built, and what a realistic path forward looks like.
speaking.topic_3_desc: Taking machine learning from a paper to a shipped, patented system inside a large organisation — and the trade-offs nobody writes up.
speaking.topic_4_title: Building a research career from the margins
speaking.topic_4_desc: For students and early-career researchers outside the traditional pipeline: how to find collaborators, publish, and be taken seriously.
speaking.invite_body: Tell me about the audience, the date and the format. I answer every enquiry, and I am glad to tailor a talk to what your group is working on.

consulting.title: Consulting & advisory
consulting.subtitle: Independent advisory for teams building with language models, document AI, or African language technology.
consulting.area_1_desc: Architecture reviews, evaluation design, and honest assessments of whether a language model is the right tool for the problem in front of you.
consulting.area_2_desc: Extraction, classification and understanding pipelines for messy real-world documents — the area of my patent work.
consulting.area_3_desc: Data strategy, community partnership and model choices for teams building products for African markets and multilingual users.
consulting.area_4_desc: For labs and foundations: research direction, publication strategy, and building collaborations that survive past the first grant cycle.
consulting.format_1_desc: One call to pressure-test a decision. Often enough.
consulting.format_2_desc: A focused review of a system, dataset or research plan, delivered as a written assessment.
consulting.format_3_desc: A recurring engagement with a team over a quarter or more.
consulting.cta_body: The first call is free and has no agenda beyond working out whether I can genuinely help. If I am not the right person, I will say so and point you to someone who is.
